Every point names the official source it comes from; each source carries the date it was checked. sections.question: Can tourists buy weed in Phoenix?
sections.short: Yes. Adults 21 and older can buy adult-use marijuana from a licensed marijuana establishment. The store checks your age against an accepted ID, which includes a driver license from any state and a passport.

points.text: Adults 21 and older may buy adult-use marijuana from a licensed marijuana establishment, and only licensed marijuana establishments may sell it.
A person 21 or older may buy one ounce or less of adult-use marijuana, of which no more than 5 grams may be concentrate.
Before a sale, the store must verify the customer’s age with one of the forms of ID that Arizona law accepts.

Accepted IDs include an unexpired driver license or nonoperating ID from any U.S. state, the District of Columbia, a U.S. territory or Canada with a photo and date of birth; an unexpired U.S. armed forces ID; a valid unexpired passport or resident alien card; a foreign consular ID that uses biometric verification; and a U.S. border crossing card.

sections.question: How do I check that a Phoenix store is licensed?
sections.short: Look it up on AZ Care Check, the Arizona Department of Health Services’ database of licensed facilities, marijuana establishments included.

points.text: AZ Care Check is the Department’s licensing history database of providers and facilities, marijuana facilities included, with any deficiencies or enforcement actions.

link.label: Look up a marijuana facility on AZ Care Check

points.text: Medical marijuana is bought only from a nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary.

sections.question: How much weed can I have in Arizona?
sections.short: Up to 1 ounce, of which no more than 5 grams can be concentrate. Having more than 1 ounce but no more than 2.5 ounces is a petty offense.

points.text: Adults 21 and older may possess, consume, buy or transport up to one ounce of marijuana, of which no more than 5 grams may be concentrate.
A store may sell a customer no more than one ounce at a time, of which no more than 5 grams may be concentrate.
Having more than one ounce but not more than 2.5 ounces, with no more than 12.5 grams of it concentrate, is a petty offense.
An adult may give up to one ounce, with no more than 5 grams of concentrate, to another adult 21 or older, as long as it is free and not advertised.

sections.question: Where can you smoke weed in Phoenix?
sections.short: In private, where the property owner allows it. Smoking marijuana in a public place or open space is not allowed, and private owners, along with the state and local governments on their own property, can ban it.

points.text: Arizona’s adult-use law does not allow anyone to smoke marijuana in a public place or open space. Doing so is a petty offense.
The Department of Health Services says marijuana may not be smoked in public.
Any private person, business or organization that occupies, owns or controls property may prohibit or regulate marijuana there.
The state, cities and other local governments may prohibit or regulate it on property they occupy, own, control or operate.

sections.question: Can I smoke weed in my Phoenix hotel room?
sections.short: Only if the hotel allows it. Arizona law lets anyone who owns or controls private property, a hotel included, ban or restrict marijuana there.

points.text: The adult-use law does not stop any private person, business or organization that occupies, owns or controls property from prohibiting or regulating marijuana on or in that property.

sections.question: Can I have weed in a car in Arizona, or drive after using it?
sections.short: Don’t use it in a running car, even as a passenger, and don’t drive if it has impaired you to even the slightest degree.

points.text: The law does not allow anyone to consume marijuana while driving, operating or riding in the passenger seat or compartment of an operating motor vehicle, boat, vessel, aircraft or other vehicle used for transportation.
It does not allow driving, flying or boating while impaired to even the slightest degree by marijuana.
An adult is not guilty of DUI only because marijuana metabolites are in their body, unless they are also impaired to the slightest degree.

sections.question: Can I take weed to Grand Canyon National Park?
sections.short: No. The National Park Service says possessing or using marijuana inside any of its parks, preserves, rivers or monuments is prohibited, because it remains illegal under federal law.

points.text: Possession or use of marijuana inside a National Park Service unit, including parks, preserves, rivers and monuments, is prohibited. Marijuana remains illegal under federal law.

sections.question: Can I fly home with weed from Phoenix?
sections.short: Not legally. TSA says marijuana remains illegal under federal law, and its officers refer anything illegal they find to law enforcement.

points.text: TSA says marijuana and some cannabis products, including some CBD oil, remain illegal under federal law unless they have no more than 0.3% THC on a dry-weight basis or are FDA-approved. Its officers don’t search for drugs, but they refer anything illegal they find to law enforcement.

sections.question: Does Arizona accept medical marijuana cards from other states?
sections.short: Yes, in part. A visiting patient’s card from another state has the same force as an Arizona card, but visiting patients can’t buy at Arizona’s medical dispensaries. Visitors 21 and older can buy at adult-use stores.

points.text: A registry card from another state that lets a visiting qualifying patient possess or use marijuana where it was issued has the same force and effect as an Arizona registry card, except that a visiting patient may not obtain marijuana from a nonprofit medical marijuana dispensary.
A visiting qualifying patient is someone who is not an Arizona resident, or has lived in Arizona for fewer than 30 days, and who was diagnosed by a person licensed to prescribe in their home state.
A registered patient 21 or older can also buy adult-use marijuana, as long as they don’t possess more than the allowed amount.

sections.question: What should I know about edibles in Arizona?
sections.short: They can look like ordinary food, drinks or candy and hold several adult doses. Keep them locked away in their original packaging, and don’t drive after using marijuana.

points.text: Edible marijuana products can look like food, drinks or candy, and can contain several times the adult dose of THC.
Store marijuana products locked away and in their original packaging.
Don’t drive after using marijuana.
If a child eats, drinks or inhales a marijuana product, call the Arizona Poison and Drug Information Center at 1-800-222-1222, or 911, right away.
